answers.question: Which quantity does Alba determine using visible light, and which quantity does it explicitly exclude?

messages.content: Which quantity does Alba determine using visible light, and which quantity does it explicitly exclude?

response.answer:
El sensor Alba determina la turbidez mediante luz visible: concretamente usa luz verde a 530 nm, y ese mismo método exige una calibración cada 30 días. [fixture 13, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aa47ee3afc37b1762e50a33565aec1a3fbd53e7575b51eec553eecdf0e89410d3%3Acd3f5c65315a284b0b27fa6b09ce914bae3bf4f53cacd8d6fcffe8e9709879eb%3A0)

En cambio, excluye explícitamente la concentración de oxígeno: no la mide. [fixture 13, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aa47ee3afc37b1762e50a33565aec1a3fbd53e7575b51eec553eecdf0e89410d3%3Acd3f5c65315a284b0b27fa6b09ce914bae3bf4f53cacd8d6fcffe8e9709879eb%3A0)

traces.draft:
Los registros de Bruma consignan una **mediana de 18** y una **media de 24** ([fixture 29](nodus://passage/documentary%3Ad5b10fa3471e1c459fadef9d4866878048600d8392170f2a47d771517f1ccace%3Affcf9c920890d5944aa0cb8d09f7f97a2cc0628e2ea5715337636e8aca4cc998%3A0)), para una encuesta de 240 personas de seis aldeas con un nivel de confianza del 95% ([fixture 09](nodus://passage/documentary%3Ad5b10fa3471e1c459fadef9d4866878048600d8392170f2a47d771517f1ccace%3A7eadaec208d03a58edf33ed36bf60f972a4b794dc7d5b0d545d86ba91b6c6bce%3A0)). Esas mismas cifras se repiten en los demás registros de la serie ([fixture 24](nodus://passage/documentary%3Ad5b10fa3471e1c459fadef9d4866878048600d8392170f2a47d771517f1ccace%3Ac8ef43ab2e2684b4ba0334a039e451ee41b25312ea813d708f55a5f3ff32c188%3A0); [fixture 04](nodus://passage/documentary%3Ad5b10fa3471e1c459fadef9d4866878048600d8392170f2a47d771517f1ccace%3Ac02ddc2ce461540728cfdbd4df28e04844d5b76e5d156433d149b67d89d98640%3A0)).

Sobre lo que permiten concluir: una versión afirma explícitamente que mediana y media «no son equivalentes» ([fixture 14](nodus://passage/documentary%3Ad5b10fa3471e1c459fadef9d4866878048600d8392170f2a47d771517f1ccace%3A9ab1d2a0152a8bc5d7aff4bd12a8f2b8d115dc2ec994fec57e77457fae6b893e%3A0)), y otra registra la misma observación junto a los métodos de encuesta ([fixture 19](nodus://passage/documentary%3Ad5b10fa3471e1c459fadef9d4866878048600d8392170f2a47d771517f1ccace%3A61434d2ac6d333a8f0819e7671caafa2f8f906a9b013e047f7e18de96b2dc4bb%3A0)). Es decir, la evidencia aportada sostiene que ambos estadísticos difieren (18 ≠ 24), pero **no establece la forma ni la asimetría de la distribución**: ningún pasaje suministrado describe cómo se reparten los datos ni explica la diferencia entre ambos valores.

Inferencia mía, no documentada: cuando la media supera a la mediana, el patrón habitual es una asimetría hacia la derecha, pero las fuentes no afirman tal cosa. Por separado, el total preliminar de 239 registros fue corregido a 240 participantes ([fixture 14](nodus://passage/documentary%3Ad5b10fa3471e1c459fadef9d4866878048600d8392170f2a47d771517f1ccace%3A9ab1d2a0152a8bc5d7aff4bd12a8f2b8d115dc2ec994fec57e77457fae6b893e%3A0)).

answers.question: Compare the interpretation limits of Vega and Bruma, distinguishing measured outcomes from unsupported conclusions.

messages.content: Compare the interpretation limits of Vega and Bruma, distinguishing measured outcomes from unsupported conclusions.

response.answer:
**Vega — lo medido y lo que no puede concluirse**

La fuente se identifica como archivo sintético. [fixture 07, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3Ace34be62f4e64bd67814a4cf354a630700db6204d6a75df37f85216dc451c53c%3A0)

**Bruma — lo medido y sus límites**

Lo medido: la encuesta incluyó 240 personas de seis pueblos; la confianza fue del 95%; la mediana era 18 y la media 24, y no son equivalentes. [fixture 14, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A9ab1d2a0152a8bc5d7aff4bd12a8f2b8d115dc2ec994fec57e77457fae6b893e%3A0) Hay además una corrección de conteo: un memorándum preliminar contó 239 registros y la corrección final 240 participantes, quedando el total preliminar superado. [fixture 04, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3Ac02ddc2ce461540728cfdbd4df28e04844d5b76e5d156433d149b67d89d98640%3A0)

**Comparación**

En Vega el límite es una variable ausente: se midieron dos proporciones de recuerdo (72% y 51%) y no se midió la inteligencia, de modo que no cabe atribuir la diferencia a esa variable. [fixture 02, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A9b844c0eefccf6f1ec9f777093e1f14b67f2fd4af60a5c330403c0fa8c814bf5%3A0) [fixture 22, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A5eba4064d35afb8d1c834b39e14dc11dd11d6d354929c067f317fe0f51244630%3A0) En Bruma lo medido son estadísticos descriptivos de una encuesta (240 personas, confianza del 95%, mediana 18, media 24) y una corrección de conteo (239 preliminar superado por 240 final); las revisiones administrativas no añaden ninguna afirmación sobre resultados. [fixture 19, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A61434d2ac6d333a8f0819e7671caafa2f8f906a9b013e047f7e18de96b2dc4bb%3A0) [fixture 14, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A9ab1d2a0152a8bc5d7aff4bd12a8f2b8d115dc2ec994fec57e77457fae6b893e%3A0)

Ambas fuentes comparten una estructura parecida: fijan cifras medidas y, junto a ellas, marcan explícitamente un límite. Pero el tipo de límite difiere.

**Vega — lo medido y lo que no puede concluirse**

El resultado medido es doble y comparativo: en el ensayo, el grupo de recuperación espaciada recordó el 72% y el de relectura, el 51% ([fixture 02](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A9b844c0eefccf6f1ec9f777093e1f14b67f2fd4af60a5c330403c0fa8c814bf5%3A0)). El mismo par de cifras aparece en otras lenguas ([fixture 17](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A9aaa5a3c4578ea511be65b4ee2fb388828c6a30c36647491bf4c371fac6bbff3%3A0); [fixture 12](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3Abcb9bdb5ab6adf9c0fff3e13b401faeaedb9c417cefb356ca363ea402dd8c254%3A0)), aunque esa repetición traducida no debe tomarse como corroboración independiente. El límite es explícito: la inteligencia no fue medida ([fixture 22](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A5eba4064d35afb8d1c834b39e14dc11dd11d6d354929c067f317fe0f51244630%3A0)), de modo que el texto no respalda atribuir la diferencia de recuerdo a la inteligencia. La fuente se identifica como archivo sintético ([fixture 07](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3Ace34be62f4e64bd67814a4cf354a630700db6204d6a75df37f85216dc451c53c%3A0)).

**Bruma — lo medido y sus límites**

Lo medido: la encuesta incluyó 240 personas de seis pueblos; la confianza fue del 95%; la mediana era 18 y la media 24, y no son equivalentes ([fixture 14](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A9ab1d2a0152a8bc5d7aff4bd12a8f2b8d115dc2ec994fec57e77457fae6b893e%3A0)). Hay además una corrección de conteo: un memorándum preliminar contó 239 registros y la corrección final 240 participantes, quedando el total preliminar superado ([fixture 04](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3Ac02ddc2ce461540728cfdbd4df28e04844d5b76e5d156433d149b67d89d98640%3A0); [fixture 09](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A7eadaec208d03a58edf33ed36bf60f972a4b794dc7d5b0d545d86ba91b6c6bce%3A0)). El límite aquí es distinto al de Vega: mediana y media no son equivalentes, así que no cabe sustituir una por la otra ni inferir una distribución a partir de esos estadísticos. Y declarar un nivel de confianza del 95% no establece por sí mismo que se calculara un intervalo.

**Comparación**

En Vega el límite es una variable ausente (inteligencia) frente a dos proporciones medidas. En Bruma el límite es la no equivalencia entre dos estadísticos y la vigencia de un conteo corregido. Ambas fuentes comparten un rasgo que condiciona su lectura: se autodescriben como archivos sintéticos ([fixture 02](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A9b844c0eefccf6f1ec9f777093e1f14b67f2fd4af60a5c330403c0fa8c814bf5%3A0); [fixture 14](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A9ab1d2a0152a8bc5d7aff4bd12a8f2b8d115dc2ec994fec57e77457fae6b893e%3A0)), por lo que sus cifras no deben extrapolarse a conclusiones causales ni a un diseño experimental real.

**Lo que Linde permite restaurar**

El endpoint `/restore` recupera elementos eliminados ([fixture 20, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A675879258dcb3e6a835b42863551a6db292065a442a236cf765cf78e9f4937a8%3A0)). Esa es toda la capacidad de restauración que describen los pasajes: elementos borrados.

**Lo que excluye**

La restauración no alcanza las cuentas cerradas ([fixture 25, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3Afbccb7ff3612d283e7bae388db6100e71002eb821965768c22fa6eacb02ffc07%3A0); [fixture 05, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3Ae661cadd9869d6310ac452888c6113170eb8f2087b0b00abcfdd8aed7b067bde%3A0); [fixture 15, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A95afb0f98bc130f1dc8d780686f3b7c7e0f754f158f307ee93cb450e65b657bf%3A0); [fixture 10, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3Acc2bc7187edf8af865a07705765f129559817376e3763ae12245b90be2789e68%3A0)). Es una exclusión explícita, no una limitación temporal: los pasajes oponen «elementos eliminados» a «cuentas cerradas» dentro de la misma frase, sin condicionar la exclusión al plazo de conservación.

**Por qué no debe mezclarse con la retención de eventos**

Son dos cantidades distintas y los textos las presentan por separado. La retención de eventos es de 14 días ([fixture 25, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3Afbccb7ff3612d283e7bae388db6100e71002eb821965768c22fa6eacb02ffc07%3A0); [fixture 20, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3A675879258dcb3e6a835b42863551a6db292065a442a236cf765cf78e9f4937a8%3A0)), y la versión 2 cambió ese plazo de 7 a 14 días ([fixture 30, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A4ad1c9e8a29fb149348cd61ef9ab4a84f5b90ff62c0e998ed28f38ae4b5e815e%3Afc8f8c7272fa2d9ff4f125062dfd320d09c5005a23030d33c84ccd9240b83c23%3A0)). Nada en los pasajes indica que ese cambio de plazo afecte a qué puede restaurarse ni a la exclusión de cuentas cerradas; ambos hechos aparecen enunciados como afirmaciones independientes. Los pasajes no establecen si existe un límite temporal para invocar `/restore` sobre un elemento eliminado.

answers.question: Explica cómo NF4, la doble cuantización y los optimizadores paginados ahorran memoria en QLoRA; distingue almacenamiento y cómputo y cita el artículo.

messages.content: Explica cómo NF4, la doble cuantización y los optimizadores paginados ahorran memoria en QLoRA; distingue almacenamiento y cómputo y cita el artículo.

response.answer:
QLoRA combina tres mecanismos para reducir el uso de memoria: el tipo de dato NF4, la doble cuantización (DQ) y los optimizadores paginados. [public QLORA001, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A0) El objetivo declarado es reducir la memoria lo suficiente para afinar un modelo de 65B parámetros en una sola GPU de 48 GB sin degradar el rendimiento frente al ajuste fino completo de 16 bits. [public QLORA001, p. 1](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A0) La reducción de memoria del ajuste de 65B pasa de >780 GB a <48 GB. [public QLORA001, pp. 1–2](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A1)

**Almacenamiento frente a cómputo.** QLoRA distingue un tipo de dato de almacenamiento de baja precisión —habitualmente 4 bits— y un tipo de dato de cómputo, habitualmente BFloat16. [public QLORA001, p. 4](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A6) Así, el ahorro de memoria recae en el almacenamiento, mientras el cómputo se mantiene en precisión de 16 bits. [public QLORA001, p. 4](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A6)

**NF4.** El tipo NormalFloat se apoya en la cuantización por cuantiles, que reparte el mismo número de valores en cada bin de cuantización. [public QLORA001, p. 4](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A6)

**Doble cuantización.** DQ cuantiza las constantes de cuantización y ahorra una media de unos 0,37 bits por parámetro, aproximadamente 3 GB en un modelo de 65B. [public QLORA001, pp. 2–3](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A3) Según el texto, DQ aporta solo ganancias menores de rendimiento, pero permite un mayor ahorro de memoria sin degradarlo. [public QLORA001, pp. 6–7](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A14)

**Optimizadores paginados.** Su función es evitar que los picos de memoria durante el *gradient checkpointing* provoquen errores de memoria insuficiente; el artículo los señala como críticos para el ajuste de 33B/65B en una sola GPU de 24/48 GB. [public QLORA001, pp. 5–6](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A11) [public QLORA001, p. 4](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A6) El presupuesto de memoria incluye el modelo base de 4 bits (5.048 MB), los parámetros LoRA (26 MB) y las entradas de gradiente con *checkpointing* (≈18 MB por secuencia de media); la tabla de huella de memoria recoge 65B en 45,0 GB y 41 GB según el modelo listado. [public QLORA001, p. 4](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A6) [public QLORA001, p. 26](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A57)

passage.text: # QLORA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs Tim Dettmers∗ Artidoro Pagnoni∗ Ari Holtzman Luke Zettlemoyer University of Washington {dettmers,artidoro,ahai,lsz}@cs.washington.edu ## Abstract We present QLORA, an efficient finetuning approach that reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance. QLORA backpropagates gradients through a frozen, 4-bit quantized pretrained language model into Low Rank Adapters (LoRA). Our best model family, which we name Guanaco, outperforms all previous openly released models on the Vicuna benchmark, reaching 99.3% of the performance level of ChatGPT while only requiring 24 hours of finetuning on a single GPU. QLORA introduces a number of innovations to save memory without sacrificing performance: (a) 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4), a new data type that is information theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights (b) Double Quantization to reduce the average memory footprint by quantizing the quantization constants, and (c) Paged Optimizers to manage memory spikes. We use QLORA to finetune more than 1,000 models, providing a detailed analysis of instruction following and chatbot performance across 8 instruction datasets, multiple model types (LLaMA, T5), and model scales that would be infeasible to run with regular finetuning (e.g. 33B and 65B parameter models). Our results show that QLoRA finetuning on a small high-quality dataset leads to state-of-the-art results, even when using smaller models than the previous SoTA. We provide a detailed analysis of chatbot performance based on both human and GPT-4 evaluations showing that GPT-4 evaluations are a cheap and reasonable alternative to human evaluation. Furthermore, we find that current chatbot benchmarks are not trustworthy to accurately evaluate the performance levels of chatbots. A lemon-picked analysis demonstrates where Guanaco fails compared to

We release all of our models and code, including CUDA kernels for 4-bit training.2 arXiv:2305.14314v1 [cs.LG] 23 May 2023 ## 1 Introduction Finetuning large language models (LLMs) is a highly effective way to improve their performance, [40, 62, 43, 61, 59, 37] and to add desirable or remove undesirable behaviors [43, 2, 4]. However, finetuning very large models is prohibitively expensive; regular 16-bit finetuning of a LLaMA 65B parameter model [57] requires more than 780 GB of GPU memory. While recent quantization methods can reduce the memory footprint of LLMs [14, 13, 18, 66], such techniques only work for inference and break down during training [65]. We demonstrate for the first time that it is possible to finetune a quantized 4-bit model without any performance degradation. Our method, QLORA, uses a novel high-precision technique to quantize a pretrained model to 4-bit, then adds a small set of learnable Low-rank Adapter weights [28] ∗Equal contribution. QLORA reduces the average memory requirements of finetuning a 65B parameter model from >780GB of GPU memory to <48GB without degrading the runtime or predictive performance compared to a 16- bit fully finetuned baseline. This marks a significant largest publicly available models to date finetunable on a single GPU.

With gradient checkpointing [9], the input gradients reduce to an average of 18 MB per sequence making them more memory intensive than all LoRA weights combined. In comparison, the 4-bit base model consumes 5,048 MB of memory. This highlights that gradient checkpointing is important but also that aggressively reducing the amount of LoRA parameter yields only minor memory benefits. This means we can use more adapters without significantly increasing the overall training memory footprint (see Appendix G for a detailed breakdown). As discussed later, this is crucial for recovering full 16-bit precision performance. ## 3 QLORA Finetuning QLORA achieves high-fidelity 4-bit finetuning via two techniques we propose—4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization and Double Quantization. Additionally, we introduce Paged Optimizers, to prevent memory spikes during gradient checkpointing from causing out-of-memory errors that have traditionally made finetuning on a single machine difficult for large models. QLORA has one low-precision storage data type, in our case usually 4-bit, and one computation data type that is usually BFloat16. In practice, this means whenever a QLORA weight tensor is used, we dequantize the tensor to BFloat16, and then perform a matrix multiplication in 16-bit. # QLORA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs Tim Dettmers∗ Artidoro Pagnoni∗ Ari Holtzman Luke Zettlemoyer University of Washington {dettmers,artidoro,ahai,lsz}@cs.washington.edu ## Abstract We present QLORA, an efficient finetuning approach that reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance. QLORA backpropagates gradients through a frozen, 4-bit quantized pretrained language model into Low Rank Adapters (LoRA). Our best model family, which we name Guanaco, outperforms all previous openly released models on the Vicuna benchmark, reaching 99.3% of the performance level of ChatGPT while only requiring 24 hours of finetuning on a single GPU. QLORA introduces a number of innovations to save memory without sacrificing performance: (a) 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4), a new data type that is information theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights (b) Double Quantization to reduce the average memory footprint by quantizing the quantization constants, and (c) Paged Optimizers to manage memory spikes. We use QLORA to finetune more than 1,000 models, providing a detailed analysis of instruction following and chatbot performance across 8 instruction datasets, multiple model types (LLaMA, T5), and model scales that would be infeasible to run with regular finetuning (e.g. 33B and 65B parameter models). Our results show that QLoRA finetuning on a small high-quality dataset leads to state-of-the-art results, even when using smaller models than the previous SoTA. We provide a detailed analysis of chatbot performance based on both human and GPT-4 evaluations showing that GPT-4 evaluations are a cheap and reasonable alternative to human evaluation. Furthermore, we find that current chatbot benchmarks are not trustworthy to accurately evaluate the performance levels of chatbots. As discussed later, this is crucial for recovering full 16-bit precision performance. ## 3 QLORA Finetuning QLORA achieves high-fidelity 4-bit finetuning via two techniques we propose—4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization and Double Quantization. Additionally, we introduce Paged Optimizers, to prevent memory spikes during gradient checkpointing from causing out-of-memory errors that have traditionally made finetuning on a single machine difficult for large models. QLORA has one low-precision storage data type, in our case usually 4-bit, and one computation data type that is usually BFloat16. In practice, this means whenever a QLORA weight tensor is used, we dequantize the tensor to BFloat16, and then perform a matrix multiplication in 16-bit. Quantile quantization works by estimating the quantile of the input tensor through the empirical cumulative distribution function. We release all of our models and code, including CUDA kernels for 4-bit training.2 arXiv:2305.14314v1 [cs.LG] 23 May 2023 ## 1 Introduction Finetuning large language models (LLMs) is a highly effective way to improve their performance, [40, 62, 43, 61, 59, 37] and to add desirable or remove undesirable behaviors [43, 2, 4]. However, finetuning very large models is prohibitively expensive; regular 16-bit finetuning of a LLaMA 65B parameter model [57] requires more than 780 GB of GPU memory. While recent quantization methods can reduce the memory footprint of LLMs [14, 13, 18, 66], such techniques only work for inference and break down during training [65]. We demonstrate for the first time that it is possible to finetune a quantized 4-bit model without any performance degradation. Our method, QLORA, uses a novel high-precision technique to quantize a pretrained model to 4-bit, then adds a small set of learnable Low-rank Adapter weights [28] ∗Equal contribution. QLORA reduces the average memory requirements of finetuning a 65B parameter model from >780GB of GPU memory to <48GB without degrading the runtime or predictive performance compared to a 16- bit fully finetuned baseline. This marks a significant largest publicly available models to date finetunable on a single GPU.

QLoRA combina tres mecanismos: el tipo de dato NF4, la doble cuantización (DQ) y los optimizadores paginados. El objetivo declarado es reducir el uso de memoria lo suficiente para afinar un modelo de 65B parámetros en una sola GPU de 48 GB sin degradar el rendimiento frente al ajuste fino completo de 16 bits ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A0)). La reducción de memoria del ajuste de 65B pasa de >780 GB a <48 GB ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A1)).

**Almacenamiento frente a cómputo.** QLoRA distingue un tipo de dato de almacenamiento de baja precisión —habitualmente 4 bits— y un tipo de dato de cómputo, habitualmente BFloat16 ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A6)). En la práctica, cada vez que se usa un tensor se desquantiza desde el almacenamiento W^NF4 al tipo de cómputo W^BF16, y la multiplicación de matrices se realiza en 16 bits ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A11)). Así, el ahorro de memoria recae en el almacenamiento, mientras el cómputo se mantiene en precisión de 16 bits.

**NF4.** El tipo NormalFloat se apoya en la cuantización por cuantiles, que reparte el mismo número de valores en cada bin de cuantización ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A6)). El artículo describe NF4 como «information theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights» ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A0)) y sostiene que NF4 mejora la precisión bit a bit frente a FP4 e Int4 ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A13)).

**Doble cuantización.** DQ cuantiza las constantes de cuantización y ahorra una media de unos 0,37 bits por parámetro, aproximadamente 3 GB en un modelo de 65B ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A3)). Según el texto, DQ aporta solo ganancias menores de rendimiento, pero permite un mayor ahorro de memoria sin degradarlo ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A13)).

**Optimizadores paginados.** Su función es evitar que los picos de memoria durante el *gradient checkpointing* provoquen errores de memoria insuficiente ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A6)); el artículo los señala como críticos para el ajuste de 33B/65B en una sola GPU de 24/48 GB ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A11)). El presupuesto de memoria incluye el modelo base de 4 bits (5.048 MB), los parámetros LoRA (26 MB) y las entradas de gradiente con *checkpointing* (≈18 MB por secuencia de media) ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A6)); la tabla de huella de memoria recoge 65B en 45,0 GB y 41 GB según el modelo listado ([Dettmers, 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3A65878fc6707a3b75b37bbddf62682462b028169ee0aca9ffacf1d88954088a84%3Acfdfc54f0eec9846a487c423f9cb54c770f4d053fd2864e96b8e3a7b51c645cb%3A57)).

# QLORA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs Tim Dettmers∗ Artidoro Pagnoni∗ Ari Holtzman Luke Zettlemoyer University of Washington {dettmers,artidoro,ahai,lsz}@cs.washington.edu ## Abstract We present QLORA, an efficient finetuning approach that reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance. QLORA backpropagates gradients through a frozen, 4-bit quantized pretrained language model into Low Rank Adapters (LoRA). Our best model family, which we name Guanaco, outperforms all previous openly released models on the Vicuna benchmark, reaching 99.3% of the performance level of ChatGPT while only requiring 24 hours of finetuning on a single GPU. QLORA introduces a number of innovations to save memory without sacrificing performance: (a) 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4), a new data type that is information theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights (b) Double Quantization to reduce the average memory footprint by quantizing the quantization constants, and (c) Paged Optimizers to manage memory spikes. We use QLORA to finetune more than 1,000 models, providing a detailed analysis of instruction following and chatbot performance across 8 instruction datasets, multiple model types (LLaMA, T5), and model scales that would be infeasible to run with regular finetuning (e.g. 33B and 65B parameter models). Our results show that QLoRA finetuning on a small high-quality dataset leads to state-of-the-art results, even when using smaller models than the previous SoTA. We provide a detailed analysis of chatbot performance based on both human and GPT-4 evaluations showing that GPT-4 evaluations are a cheap and reasonable alternative to human evaluation. Furthermore, we find that current chatbot benchmarks are not trustworthy to accurately evaluate the performance levels of chatbots. We release all of our models and code, including CUDA kernels for 4-bit training.2 arXiv:2305.14314v1 [cs.LG] 23 May 2023 ## 1 Introduction Finetuning large language models (LLMs) is a highly effective way to improve their performance, [40, 62, 43, 61, 59, 37] and to add desirable or remove undesirable behaviors [43, 2, 4]. However, finetuning very large models is prohibitively expensive; regular 16-bit finetuning of a LLaMA 65B parameter model [57] requires more than 780 GB of GPU memory. While recent quantization methods can reduce the memory footprint of LLMs [14, 13, 18, 66], such techniques only work for inference and break down during training [65]. We demonstrate for the first time that it is possible to finetune a quantized 4-bit model without any performance degradation. Our method, QLORA, uses a novel high-precision technique to quantize a pretrained model to 4-bit, then adds a small set of learnable Low-rank Adapter weights [28] ∗Equal contribution. [^2]https://github.com/artidoro/qlora and https://github.com/TimDettmers/bitsandbytes Preprint. Under review. that are tuned by backpropagating gradients through the quantized weights. QLORA reduces the average memory requirements of finetuning a 65B parameter model from >780GB of GPU memory to <48GB without degrading the runtime or predictive performance compared to a 16- bit fully finetuned baseline. This marks a significant largest publicly available models to date finetunable on a single GPU.

With gradient checkpointing [9], the input gradients reduce to an average of 18 MB per sequence making them more memory intensive than all LoRA weights combined. In comparison, the 4-bit base model consumes 5,048 MB of memory. This highlights that gradient checkpointing is important but also that aggressively reducing the amount of LoRA parameter yields only minor memory benefits. This means we can use more adapters without significantly increasing the overall training memory footprint (see Appendix G for a detailed breakdown). As discussed later, this is crucial for recovering full 16-bit precision performance. ## 3 QLORA Finetuning QLORA achieves high-fidelity 4-bit finetuning via two techniques we propose—4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization and Double Quantization. Additionally, we introduce Paged Optimizers, to prevent memory spikes during gradient checkpointing from causing out-of-memory errors that have traditionally made finetuning on a single machine difficult for large models. QLORA has one low-precision storage data type, in our case usually 4-bit, and one computation data type that is usually BFloat16. In practice, this means whenever a QLORA weight tensor is used, we dequantize the tensor to BFloat16, and then perform a matrix multiplication in 16-bit. Quantile quantization works by estimating the quantile of the input tensor through the empirical cumulative distribution function. In comparison, the 4-bit base model consumes 5,048 MB of memory. Additionally, we introduce Paged Optimizers, to prevent memory spikes during gradient checkpointing from causing out-of-memory errors that have traditionally made finetuning on a single machine difficult for large models. QLORA has one low-precision storage data type, in our case usually 4-bit, and one computation data type that is usually BFloat16. response.answer: No puedo establecer quién financió la compra de los libros de Puerto Claro: los extractos recuperados no mencionan financiación, donaciones ni adquisiciones bibliográficas.
